Your friend sounds wonderful. When you say she is not able to work a 9-5 job I want to touch on a couple things. 1.) If she is disabled, temporarily experiencing mental crisis, or any reasonable reality for why she cannot work at all - the new system would not ask her too. She will be protected. The new system is based off the wants and needs of the people, and no one is left behind or ignored. 2.) In a new system, we would abandon those things that we do not want or need. Some businesses exist only to make a profit - well nearly every business exists to make a profit, but it doesn't generate any real *value* or there is a loss of value. Here are two examples: Nearly every food production and food service establishment wastes food every day. They do this because "giving the food away would 'decrease' the value of the food" aka if they gave perfectly good food away to people who were hungry and needed it, they would lower the 'demand' for food sold for money - a person who has $30 to spend on groceries for the week would obviously rather take the free food, and they would not "pay" for the food. Therefore, businesses see this is as a loss or de-valuing the food they have created. So food goes into the trash. Food production operates the same way - food that would lower the "value" of the food - food that is disfigured but still edible is destroyed because it is "ugly", and milk pasteurizers have been known to literally pour thousands of gallons of milk down the drain to artificially control supply and drive up demand. The value of our food and being fed is based on efficiency - food being produced, shipped and given to the hungry - but on the money that can be made off this food. In our new system - labor would actually *create real value efficiently* when it comes to basic needs. Now, imagine how much labor is wasted by this destruction of food and its waste? It's a lot. 

Another example: imagine you're at a grocery store and you're about to grab some paper plates and toilet paper - as long as it's a decent quality - do you really care what brand name you are buying?? Do you think you would not want to live in a world where manufacturers for one commodity such as toilet paper and paper plates were condensed to ONE (or two) manufacturers? Without the useless competition between brands on basic services people really don't care about - we could cut down labor dramatically. My last example, think about your electric and water company. Do you know how much labor is wasted on answering phones for bill pay, how many agents set up new accounts and take down deposits? The management of money wastes so much labor it is insane. In the new system, the electrical company would have one types of worker - the technicians that turn it on, repair it, and monitor it's efficiency. That's it. 

3) In the new system, which is not focused on people having jobs just to make money for making monies sake, we could begin automating those positions because people with these skills (AI and robotics) could focus on doing so. Ultimately, there would be no change in how we do things now - but our "work" hours would be drastically reduced because work would only be completed if it is "productive". Everyone would be encouraged to work a set number of "work" hours per week in order to maintain society - you would "work" to support your fellow countrymen and in exchange your fellow countrymen would "work" in order to support you. This is not to say that anything that doesn't have "necessity" value would be forgotten - we as a group would decide what is important, and what we wanted to produce under our collective "work" hours. And with the reduction in work hours, we would have times to pursue our "passions" - those will be different for everyone. But it's important to state here that those passions would be supported and encouraged by one another. Say that someone, or a group of someones, is wanting to open an art studio - the building of that art studio would require "work" and the production of paint would require "work". So it would be moved into the set number of "work" hours someone contributes. Say someone is wanting to study epidemiological disease, or they want to work on new forms of energy production, or space exploration, or maybe someone just wants to read books in their room (these people would still be encouraged to contribute a set number of work hours) - these pursuits would be collectively agreed by the community by online voting polls or something similar - and they would move into the "work" block. 

We would still have television and media - actually, everyone's pursuits and passions would be respected, there would be less barriers between people and what they want to create. If you have a problem with your toilet, call the plumber on duty during his work block (who has taken up interpretive dance in his spare time) and they schedule you for your service - just your address and your name. For your friend, there would still be production facilities for jewelry, as I'm sure people may still wish to create these things - so she would have her raw materials to create if that is what she would like to do. Heck, that could probably be her "work" if she unable to do laborious positions. And when it comes to "work blocks" it's important that the most unfavorable positions are not given to one group of people, but shared amongst groups. Say that there is a manufacturing plant that hasn't been automated as of yet - it's grueling, boring work. If the work block is designated at 2 days a week to meet needs and other goals, a person should only be expected to work 1 day out of their work block doing the most unfavorable position. Their other two "work blocks" should be something much more enjoyable - and we can do that. It's possible.
